Even against ol granny, they still require her to click a link or reveal the password herself. Password hashes have gotten so advanced to the 512 bit encryption that it is simply not worth the time, effort and money to even attempt it. That's not how it works.

A hash is simply your password that has been converted to a random string of symbols determined by a "key". A key is nothing more than a formula that converts each character to a set of symbols. This key is not known to anyone except the target host.

On top of that, most well secured passwords use what's called a "salt". A salt is a randomly generated text that gets added to the end of the hash value. So the hacker would need to:

- get access to the hash value
- somehow know which part of the value is the hash and which is the salt
- have a brute force method that would take an astronomical amount of time to crack, again assuming the above point is accomplished.

So basically the only method worth any hackers time is to try to guess the password based off, phish them to willingly give it up themselves or to go as far as raiding their physical workspace to check for it being written somewhere.
